title: Act III, Scene II

teacherSummary.text: Hamlet coaches the players, praises Horatio and asks him to watch Claudius. During the play The Murder of Gonzago (renamed The Mousetrap), Hamlet makes bawdy jests to Ophelia and comments. When the poisoner pours poison in the king's ear, Claudius rises and leaves. Hamlet is elated. Rosencrantz and Guildenstern summon him to his mother; Hamlet mocks them with a recorder.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “suit the action to the word, the word to the action” slowly and put it in my own words: Hamlet tells the players to suit their actions to their words and their words to their actions. Next, craft. I notice the mirrored phrasing, which itself matches word and action. The strongest word is “action”: it names exactly what Hamlet himself struggles to take. Then, effect. What advice does Hamlet give the actors? My answer: Hamlet advises the actors to suit the action to the word and not overact; his advice about natural acting also comments on his own problem, since he speaks endlessly but does not act.
